excerpt_i18n.en: (Leiphone) Summary: "Benchmark leadership is just an appetizer; production-grade delivery is the real test." In June 2026, an open-source model named Boogu-Image-0.1 appeared on HuggingFace and quickly ignited the AI community after being uploaded. What made it most striking was that with a mere 10B parameters, it surpassed many larger models on several key capabilities. Bigger means stronger — this has long been an unshakable truth in AI, true for language models and image models alike. But on the Qwen-Image-Bench benchmark, the 10B Boogu-Image-0.1 scored 53.58, ahead of the 20B Qwen-Image-2512 (52.06) and the 80B Hunyuan-Image-3.0 (50.81). Outperforming rivals with 1/8 or even 1/2 of their parameter counts — even by just a few points — is enough to explain the industry's attention. Of course, benchmark scores are only one aspect of evaluating a model. More than benchmark results, what we care about is how far this dark horse model, punching above its weight, can go in real content production workflows. Do its advantages only hold up on benchmarks? Can it quickly generate photorealistic assets and compose poster layouts?

The model delivers comprehensive upgrades in generation duration, multimodal understanding, and editing precision, and is now available across ByteDance products including Doubao, Jimeng, Coze, and Xiaoyunque. It will also be opened to enterprise users in the near future via Volcano Engine. Compared with Seedance 2.0 released earlier this year, Seedance 2.5 has achieved breakthroughs in four core capabilities. Single-generation video duration has been extended to 30 seconds, with high-fidelity temporal extension capabilities that maintain character, scene, and camera consistency over longer sequences. It supports up to 50 multimodal reference materials and adds white-box model and green screen reference capabilities, making complex projects and industrial-grade creation more controllable. The model also introduces video local editing capabilities, enabling precise modifications to background, product, character, and other local elements while preserving the overall visual rhythm. Additionally, it natively supports more than 10 languages and strengthens complex instruction control, adapting to multilingual, multi-version industrial production needs. excerpt_i18n.en: The pipeline from data processing to Agent is being dramatically compressed. On July 30, reporters learned that Tencent Cloud officially launched AI DLC, an intelligent data lake computing platform, targeting AI scenarios such as autonomous driving, embodied intelligence, and Agent, providing integrated capabilities covering data processing, training, inference, and Agent applications. Taking Tencent's self-developed WorkBuddy as an example, after integrating AI DLC, its end-to-end time for processing the same batch of data was reduced by 80%, and the computing power required to complete the same tasks was about one-fifth of the previous amount. (Tencent Cloud Intelligent Lake Computing AI DLC Architecture) For a long time, enterprises developing AI applications typically needed to first use Spark for data cleaning and processing, then write the results to storage, with AI teams using frameworks such as Ray for training and inference. Different stages ran on different platforms, requiring repeated data movement, with permissions, metadata, and computing resources also managed separately. To address this pain point, AI DLC enables Spark and Ray to run on the same platform. Spark handles large-scale data processing and feature preparation, while Ray handles multimodal data processing, model training, online inference, and Agent tasks. The two frameworks share data, computing power, and permission systems, so data can directly enter training and inference after processing is complete, without cross-platform movement. AI DLC adopts a Serverless architecture, where computing power can elastically scale on a per-task basis in seconds.
